_comment: Mod -> category registry. Drives which chapter group a module's chapter
lands in, so a book with twenty mod chapters organises itself instead of
CLASSIFY BY SCALE FIRST, THEME SECOND.
The useful question is not 'what is this mod about' but 'how much game is
in it'. Waystones is navigation and Easy Villagers is automation, but both
are conveniences layered onto vanilla -- next to Mekanism or AE2 the gap in
content is so wide that filing them by theme buries the real content mods
So: anything that mostly removes friction from vanilla goes in 'qol',
whatever it is thematically. The thematic groups are for mods that add a
progression system of their own -- new resources, machines, tiers, bosses,
dimensions. If you are unsure, ask whether the mod could carry a ten-quest
chapter on its own content. If not, it is qol.
Edited by hand. Add a mod here before writing a module for it, and
validate.py will check the module's chapter_group agrees with this.
Group titles must not contain a bare '&': FTB Library reads it as a
formatting code. Write '\\&' or, better, avoid it.

vanilla.label: Vanilla
vanilla.note: No mods required; works in any pack.

qol.label: Quality of Life
qol.note: Conveniences layered onto vanilla, regardless of theme. Navigation, inventory, lighting, villager handling -- if it removes friction rather than adding a progression system, it belongs here.

food.label: Food and Farming
food.note: Crops, cooking, animals and the kitchen.

exploration.label: Exploration
exploration.note: Mods that add places to go and things to find -- new dimensions, structures, biomes. Not minimaps or waypoints; those are qol.

automation.label: Automation
automation.note: Mods with a real production chain -- machines, power, tiers. Not single-block conveniences; those are qol.

adventure.label: Adventure
adventure.note: Combat, progression systems, dimensions and bosses.

other.label: Other Mods
other.note: Fallback for anything not yet classified.
